searchText: Hello, I just wanted to share a few metrics that we have gathered from the Eth2 Main net over the past few days, using the network crawler that we are developing the data was colected over the last weekend ofcourse this is not the entire network, just a small snapshot of it, basically just the peers the crawler connected with during that test I'm a bit surprised by the peer count per client. Basic dumps of local peerstores have generally shown a prysm dominance How are you calcuating this? libp2p identify protocol? Prysm nodes being less than Lighthouse and Teku would be a big surprise. Something wrong with the data collection there. Note that prysm notes for a long time were declining incoming connections too aggressively, due to strict peer limits instead of maintaining elasticity like other clients Compare discovery data (prysm has a different default port) with that chart, and it's the complete opposite yeah, this is not the peerstore, it is only peers we managed to connect with Prysm nodes indeed have more strict peer limit parameters Also, overall Teku and Lighthouse are the clients that usually accept more connections also we might have left some ports closed during the run, so yes, this is not representative of the network, we will keep updating the figures with longer runs <@!363800010518822915> Do prysm nodes still have a hard cap on peers? Or is there some upward flexibility beyond the "target" number The default max peer count is set to 30. Prysm has a flag `--p2p-max-peers` to set custom peer count. We have been recommending 75 to nodes in certain regions to have better connectivity to others but is `--p2p-max-peers` still a strict max? it's recommended that there be some elasticity above the number with downward pruning to the target otherwise, the p2p network can become very rigid and it hard to connect to peers as a new node (also makes this type of crawling not work well) I think we touched on this in a public call a couple ago, but not sure if it made it's way to you Ah i see. I'm 99% sure it's a strict max (perspective from my running node). I'll confirm with the team and come back if not. I agree on logic to handle `elasticity above the number with downward pruning to the target` and prysm should have this. Timeline wise, I think this will be done in Jan as ppl are going to holidays we missed the call, thanks for the reminder on this! It hasnt been a strict max for a while, there is an allowance for inbound peers to connect with a node. There have been some issues with the latest libp2p update in the latest release so still investigating that
